title: Cool, Cool, Cool, Palmer Luckey and Ben Lamm Made a Genetically Modified Military Dog Startup
gist: Warhound, a Texas startup created by Anduril's Palmer Luckey and Colossal Biosciences' Ben Lamm, has raised $200M to gene-edit and clone elite US working dogs for the military, police and first responders, with the goal of reducing reliance on European breeders. The first puppies are expected in early 2027, and the dogs will carry Anduril gear. The CEO is former DoD CDO David Spirk, and investors include In-Q-Tel, Sequoia and ARK Invest.

insights.claim: Warhound, a startup from Anduril's Palmer Luckey and Colossal Biosciences cofounder Ben Lamm, has raised $200 million to rebuild America's domestic supply of elite working dogs and reduce military dependence on European dog breeders.
insights.speaker: Kate Knibbs
insights.so_what: Defense-tech capital is moving into biotech supply chains under the same onshoring argument used for hardware.
insights.quote: rebuild America’s domestic supply of elite working dogs
insights.locator: Warhound is the brainchild of Anduril’s

insights.claim: Warhound's investors include In-Q-Tel, Sequoia Capital and ARK Invest. Its CEO is David Spirk, a former Department of Defense chief data officer who most recently worked at Palantir. Colossal Biosciences holds an ownership stake, while neither Luckey nor Anduril holds equity.
insights.speaker: Kate Knibbs
insights.so_what: Colossal gains a defense-revenue spinout, and backing from In-Q-Tel signals interest from the intelligence community.
insights.locator: Neither Luckey nor Lamm will be involved

insights.claim: Warhound has collected blood samples from top-performing US military, police and first-responder dogs to clone them, mostly Belgian Malinois with some labs and shepherds. Gene editing of the first batch is under way, and the first puppies are expected in early 2027.
insights.speaker: Ben Lamm
insights.so_what: The early-2027 litter is the first milestone for checking whether Colossal-style editing can work commercially.

insights.claim: Warhound's first gene edits will target breed health conditions such as hip dysplasia. Ben Lamm later envisions adding wolf olfactory receptor genes to enhance military dogs, building on Colossal's Dire Wolf De-Extinction Project.
insights.speaker: Ben Lamm
insights.so_what: Colossal's de-extinction platform is being repurposed for defense applications.

insights.claim: Warhound dogs will be equipped with Anduril's cybernetic Augments, software and battlefield situational awareness. Ben Lamm says this currently means tools like advanced body armor rather than computers embedded in the dogs.
insights.speaker: Ben Lamm
insights.so_what: This adds another channel for Anduril's product ecosystem beyond drones and sensors.
insights.quote: Anduril’s advanced cybernetic Augments, software, and battlefield situational awareness

insights.claim: Warhound plans to operate under the guidance of the American Humane Society. WIRED's coverage is openly sardonic about the ethics of gene-enhanced military dogs.
insights.speaker: Kate Knibbs
insights.so_what: Animal-welfare and bioethics backlash is a headline risk for the venture and its backers.
insights.quote: the definitely not terrifying mission of creating genetically enhanced dogs
